_source:
Mined read-only from the zeldaret/tww decompilation at Z:/memRip/sources/tww and cross-checked against the ripped GZLE01 (Wind Waker USA) placement data at Z:/3d ripper/out/rip/GZLE01/godot/stage_data.json. THIS FILE IS THE RULES LAYER: scoring, timers, thresholds, costs, attempt limits, failure conditions and prize tiers. The STEP layer - which event plays, which trigger fires it, which room it happens in - lives in gcrip/data/ww_story_minigames.json and is NOT repeated here; each entry's story_steps field names the step ids there that it sits underneath. Where a minigame has no step in that file (auction, joy_pendant, beedle_point_card, savage_labyrinth, nintendo_gallery, salvage_corp, rito_mail_sorting) story_steps is empty and this file is the only record. TWO NOTES ON THE BRIEF THIS FILE ANSWERS: (1) the brief asked for the "Bomb Island cannon game"; there is no cannon game on Bomb Island. The only daCanon_c in the whole game outside the E3 demo stage sits on Spectacle Island, sea room 10, next to Salvatore/Kg2, and that is what the "cannon_game" entry covers. (2) The brief asked for "Salvage Corp diving"; the Salvage Corp themselves are only a daObjIkada_c barge with no game logic, so the "salvage_corp" entry covers the salvage system they represent - the Grappling Hook haul, its depth rule, its six marker kinds and its per-save randomisation. One BONUS entry that was not on the brief is included, "rito_mail_sorting": it turned up while tracing which minigame owns event register 0x8AFF, its actor is fully decompiled, and every threshold and payout in it is readable. 

HOW WIND WAKER STORES MINIGAME STATE. There is no per-minigame save area. Persistent counters are EVENT REGISTERS: they live in the same 256-byte event-flag array as the event bits (dSv_event_c { u8 mFlags[0x100]; }, include/d/d_save.h:696-710) and are addressed by the same u16 id, but the LOW BYTE of the id is a multi-bit MASK instead of a single-bit mask. src/d/d_save.cpp:1201-1210: setEventReg(id, v) does mFlags[id>>8] = (mFlags[id>>8] & ~(id & 0xFF)) | v, and getEventReg(id) returns mFlags[id>>8] & (id & 0xFF). Neither accessor shifts, so a 0xFF mask is a whole 0-255 byte, a 0x0F mask is a 0-15 value in the low nibble and a 0x03 mask is a 0-3 value in the low two bits. isEventBit() on a register id returns true when ANY masked bit is set, so a remake that models event flags as named booleans will silently corrupt every score in this file; the storage has to be the raw 256-byte array. Registers used below: 0x86FF Beedle points, 0xC0FF Joy Pendants given, 0x7F0F Knight's Crests sold, 0xAAFF Boating Course difficulty, 0xBEFF Sploosh Kaboom record, 0x790F auction winner, 0xCD03 auction item, 0xA9FF last photo shown to Carlov, and the seventeen figurine bytes 0x80FF-0x84FF / 0x8CFF-0x95FF / 0x9CFF / 0xB1FF.

OTHER SAVE AREAS THE RULES TOUCH. dSv_ocean_c { u16 field_0x0[50]; } (include/d/d_save.h:685-694, src/d/d_save.cpp:1163-1183) is 16 bits per sea grid and remembers which salvage points have been emptied. dSv_player_map_c (include/d/d_save.h:410-437, src/d/d_save.cpp:851-960) holds four 128-bit chart arrays - field_0x0[1]=GetMap, [2]=OpenMap, [3]=CompleteMap - plus mFmapBits[49], one byte per sea grid whose bit 0 is 'arrived here' and bit 1 is the GBA-link copy. dSv_player_info_c::mRandomSalvagePoint (include/d/d_save.h:468) is the per-file randomised salvage slot.

HONESTY. Every constant below carries the file:line it was read from. Actors whose bodies are /* Nonmatching */ stubs in the decomp contribute nothing but symbol names, and where that is the case the entry says so and leaves the number out rather than guessing. Nothing in this file was taken from a guide, a wiki or memory.

_confidence_legend.high: read directly out of a decompiled function body or a static table; the numbers are the game's numbers.
_confidence_legend.medium: the storage, the trigger or the surrounding wiring is decompiled but one link in the chain (usually the NPC that orders the event) is a stub, so the interpretation is inferred.
_confidence_legend.low: the actor is a stub or the data is placement-only; the entry names the actor and the archive and says what could not be recovered.

auction.name: The Windfall Island Auction
auction.stage: Orichh (Windfall auction house interior). Placement: one Auction actor (the auctioneer) plus eight bidder actors Auc0..Auc7, eleven Fdai pedestals, one takara2 chest, and the NPCs Gp1/Kp1/Kf1/Bm4 (out/rip/GZLE01/godot/stage_data.json:Orichh).
auction.actor: daAuction_c, src/d/actor/d_a_auction.cpp - FULLY DECOMPILED, zero stub bodies. The rival bidders' own actor daNpcAuction_c (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_auction.cpp) is a stub but holds no rules; daAuction_c drives the whole auction including every rival's bid.
auction.cost: No entry fee. You pay only what you bid, and only if you win: on the winning message the auctioneer calls dComIfGp_setItemRupeeCount(-mCurrBid) (src/d/actor/d_a_auction.cpp:1444). A bid is refused if dComIfGs_getRupee() < the entered amount (src/d/actor/d_a_auction.cpp:1339-1343) or if it is not strictly greater than the current bid (src/d/actor/d_a_auction.cpp:1344-1348); both refusals play JA_SE_AUC_BID_NG.
rules: A round auctions exactly one item. Which item is picked: if event bit 0x4008 is set - meaning the previous round was won by a rival and is being re-run - the item is re-read from register 0xCD03 and the opening bid is raised by 10. Otherwise getItemNo() picks uniformly at random among the entries of l_item_dat whose obtained-bit is not yet set (src/d/actor/d_a_auction.cpp:413-424, 1488-1508).

getItemNo() has a real off-by-one in the shipped game: the counting loop runs i<4 over all four items but the picking loop runs only i<3, so index 3 (the Piece of Heart) is returned only as the fall-through when the random draw does not land on an earlier unobtained item (src/d/actor/d_a_auction.cpp:1488-1508). Reproduce the loop exactly rather than 'fixing' it.

The round is a countdown, not a turn limit. eventStartInit() creates a dTimer_c of 60 seconds for a normal auction and 30 seconds for the second-tier auction (m822 == 2) (src/d/actor/d_a_auction.cpp:643-651).

Six rival bidders (l_npc_dat indices 1..6; index 0 is Link's own row) bid on their own timers. Each rival has a wait rate pair, a bid-increment range and a hard spending limit; a rival stops bidding the moment mCurrBid reaches its limit (src/d/actor/d_a_auction.cpp:67-75, 890-909, 1015-1033).
A rival's raise is mCurrBid += rate * (mBidIncMin + rndF(mBidIncMax - mBidIncMin)); in the late-auction branch the increment is doubled (src/d/actor/d_a_auction.cpp:908, 1033).
The seating order of the six rivals is shuffled at construction: 100 random swaps over m80C[1..6] (src/d/actor/d_a_auction.cpp:198-208).

Link bids by entering a number. It must be <= his rupee count and > the current bid. When Link outbids a rival by a wide margin the rivals hesitate: if the new bid >= mCurrBid * l_after_bet_rate[m82C] AND mCurrBid >= l_after_bet_chk[m82C], the next rival bid is delayed by 60 * (l_after_bet_wait[m82C][0] + rnd(l_after_bet_wait[m82C][1] - [0])) frames (src/d/actor/d_a_auction.cpp:1362-1368).

Three warning stages fire as the clock runs down, at the l_rest_msg_time1 / l_rest_msg_time2 thresholds in milliseconds, each with its own message and sound (JA_SE_AUC_LAST_SPURT, JA_SE_AUC_FEW_TIME, JA_SE_AUC_5_SEC) (src/d/actor/d_a_auction.cpp:126-151, 935-970, 1044-1079). time1 is used for the 60 s auction, time2 for the 30 s one.

When the clock hits zero the highest bidder wins. If a rival won (m824 != 0) the auctioneer sets bit 0x4008, stores the winner's model number in register 0x790F and the item index in register 0xCD03, and deletes the item actor - that is the 'someone else bought it, come back' state which makes the next round re-auction the same item 10 rupees dearer. If Link won, bit 0x4008 is cleared (src/d/actor/d_a_auction.cpp:1423-1436).
On a Link win the item is created by fopAcM_createItemForPresentDemo and its obtained event bit is set, so each of the four prizes can be won exactly once (src/d/actor/d_a_auction.cpp:1194-1212).

The second-tier auction (m822 == 2, mCurrAuctionItemIndex &= 1) auctions the two statues in l_item_dat2, but hands over the SUBSTITUTE items in l_item_dat22 - Magic Armor for the Postman Statue slot and Treasure Chart 6 for the Shop Guru Statue slot - while still setting the l_item_dat2 obtained-bit (src/d/actor/d_a_auction.cpp:432-441, 1195-1202). That is how the auction pays out once the statues themselves are already owned.
dComIfGp_startMiniGame(5) marks the play struct while an auction runs (src/d/actor/d_a_auction.cpp:426, 440).

value.who: Link's own row (never bids on its own)

rewards._storage: One event bit per prize, set the moment the item is created. Plus register 0x790F (byte 0x79, mask 0x0F) = which rival won the outstanding item, and register 0xCD03 (byte 0xCD, mask 0x03) = which item is outstanding; both only meaningful while bit 0x4008 is set.

tiers.item: Postman Statue (second-tier slot 0; actually hands over dItemNo_MAGIC_ARMOR_e = 0x2A)
Shop Guru Statue (second-tier slot 1; actually hands over dItemNo_COLLECT_MAP_06_e = 0xF9)

register.0x790F: winning rival's model number (byte 0x79, low nibble)
register.0xCD03: outstanding item index 0-3 (byte 0xCD, low two bits)
register.0x4008: bit: an item is outstanding, i.e. a rival won it and it will be re-auctioned

joy_pendant.name: Mrs. Marie's Joy Pendant collection
joy_pendant.stage: Nitiyou (the Windfall Island schoolhouse). Mrs. Marie is the only Ho actor there (out/rip/GZLE01/godot/stage_data.json:Nitiyou); a second Ho stands in the test stage K_Test6.
joy_pendant.actor: daNpc_Ho_c, src/d/actor/d_a_npc_ho.cpp - FULLY DECOMPILED, zero stub bodies.
joy_pendant.cost: Free. This is a hand-in, not a purchase. Pendants come from Peahats, Boko Babas and the Killer Bees; the stock is the beast counter dBeastIdx_JOY_PENDANT_e (beast index 7).
rules: Two counters, not one. dComIfGs_getBeastNum(dBeastIdx_JOY_PENDANT_e) is how many pendants Link is carrying right now; event register 0xC0FF (byte 0xC0, whole byte) is the running TOTAL ever handed in. The tiers are gated on the total, the payouts on the amount handed over in one go.

receivePendant(n): reads register 0xC0FF, subtracts n from the beast counter, adds n to the total, CLAMPS the total at 99 and hands the overflow back to the beast counter, then writes the total back (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_ho.cpp:70-82). The clamp means pendant 100 and beyond cannot be given away, and in VERSION_DEMO the overflow was simply destroyed.
First hand-in is a single pendant, hard-coded: msg 0x273D calls receivePendant(1) and pays a Red Rupee (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_ho.cpp:290-292, 305-309).

The twenty-pendant offer only appears once Link is CARRYING at least 20: msg 0x273E branches to 0x2741 when getBeastNum >= 20 (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_ho.cpp:293-299). Accepting calls receivePendant(20) and pays the Cabana Deed, setting bit 0x1C08 (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_ho.cpp:310-320).

The Hero's Charm is offered when the TOTAL register 0xC0FF has reached 40 (0x28) and bit 0x1C04 is not yet set (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_ho.cpp:329-334); accepting sets bit 0x1C04 (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_ho.cpp:349-355).

After both prizes are taken, every further hand-in gives all carried pendants at once and pays by how many were handed over: fewer than 3 -> Red Rupee, fewer than 5 -> Purple Rupee, 5 or more -> Orange Rupee (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_ho.cpp:336-348).
Once the total reaches 99 (0x63) the conversation goes to message 0x275E instead of the hand-in branch - the collection is closed (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_ho.cpp:420-423).

Which conversation opens is chosen by getMsg(): night stops the whole thing (0x2722), the very first ever talk sets bit 0x1E01 and plays 0x2711, and thereafter the greeting is 0x2712 when the total is 0 and 0x2713 when it is not (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_ho.cpp:386-398).
The pendant Link is wearing is a separate model on Mrs. Marie's backbone joint, drawn only while register 0xC0FF != 0 (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_ho.cpp:763-771).

Mrs. Marie must first be rescued from the Killer Bees: the whole hand-in branch requires bit 0x1E04 (0x1E02 in the demo build) and the pre-item to be a Joy Pendant (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_ho.cpp:401-404).

beast_index.value: dBeastIdx_JOY_PENDANT_e (7 - the literal 7 is passed to setItemBeastNumCount)

tiers.prize: Red Rupee (dItemNo_RED_RUPEE_e = 0x04, 20 rupees)

tiers.when: hand over 20 pendants in one go (requires carrying >= 20)
tiers.prize: Cabana Deed (dItemNo_CABANA_DEED_e = 0x9C)

tiers.when: total handed in reaches 40 and the Cabana Deed is already taken
tiers.prize: Hero's Charm (dItemNo_HEROS_CHARM_e = 0x43)
Red Rupee (0x04)
Purple Rupee (dItemNo_PURPLE_RUPEE_e = 0x05, 50 rupees)

tiers.when: afterwards, handing over 5 or more pendants
tiers.prize: Orange Rupee (dItemNo_ORANGE_RUPEE_e = 0x06, 100 rupees)

tiers.when: one-off, unrelated to the count: the rescue conversation
tiers.prize: Purple Rupee (0x05)
tiers.bit: 0x1F80 gates it; 0x2201 and 0x1340 are its prerequisites

beedle_point_card.name: Beedle's Shop Ship membership point card
beedle_point_card.stage: Obshop (the interior of Beedle's shop ship). The exterior hulls are daObjIkada_c ship types (src/d/actor/d_a_obj_ikada.cpp:1-4).
beedle_point_card.actor: daNpc_Bs1_c, src/d/actor/d_a_npc_bs1.cpp - one stub body out of ~2200 lines; the whole point-card path is decompiled. mType 0 is the ordinary Beedle, mType != 0 is Masked Beedle on the Shop Ships (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_bs1.cpp:2142-2151).
beedle_point_card.cost: Whatever the item costs. The point is the by-product: one point per completed purchase, regardless of price.
rules: Register 0x86FF (byte 0x86, whole byte) is the point count. Every completed purchase adds exactly 1 and the total is clamped at 255 (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_bs1.cpp:940-942). There is no per-item point value.
At exactly 30 points a Silver Membership letter is posted (dLetter_send(LETTER_SILVER_MEMBERSHIP = 0xB003)) and the shopkeeper plays message 0xF50 (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_bs1.cpp:955-962).
At exactly 60 points a Gold Membership letter is posted (dLetter_send(LETTER_GOLD_MEMBERSHIP = 0xAF03)) and the shopkeeper plays 0xF53 (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_bs1.cpp:944-953).
Both awards are on the '==' branch only. Points above 60 fall straight through to the ordinary next-purchase message; there is no third tier (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_bs1.cpp:944-947).

Once points >= 60 the card is treated as full: the greeting, the default message and the 'buy something else?' prompt all branch to the card-full variants (0xF5C/0xF5D, 0xF60, 0xF61) (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_bs1.cpp:691-694, 1055-1060, 1237-1239).
The message system prints the current point count as a substitution in Beedle's text (src/f_op/f_op_msg_mng.cpp:2545, 4667, 6742, 8591).

A SEPARATE counter, register 0x7F0F (byte 0x7F, mask 0x0F, so 0-15), counts Knight's Crests sold to Masked Beedle. It is incremented by the number sold and clamped at 15; below 10 the seller gets the ordinary message 0xFD5, and the first time it reaches 10 with bit 0x3B04 clear the bit is set and message 0xFD6 plays - that is the Hurricane Spin hand-over (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_bs1.cpp:585-604, 1013-1018).
Masked Beedle's stock rotation is driven by register 0xBB07 (byte 0xBB, mask 0x07, so 0-7) (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_bs1.cpp:1108-1125).

Selling monster parts uses the beast counters, not points: Green/Blue Chu Jelly, Joy Pendants, Golden Feathers and Knight's Crests each have their own message block and their own dBeastIdx (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_bs1.cpp:560-583, 1000-1012).
One-off: the first time Link owns a Bomb Bag while bombs are in stock, bit 0x1F20 is set and Beedle plays 0xF55 (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_bs1.cpp:1047-1052).

tiers.prize: Silver Membership Card, delivered by post
Gold Membership Card, delivered by post

tiers.when: 10 Knight's Crests sold to Masked Beedle
tiers.prize: message 0xFD6 hand-over (the Hurricane Spin lesson); the item itself is created outside this branch

nintendo_gallery.name: The Nintendo Gallery figurine quota
nintendo_gallery.stage: Eight rooms: Pfigure (the entrance hall, where Carlov works) plus figureA..figureG. Placed Figure actors: figureA 24, figureB 27, figureC 14, figureD 18, figureE 19, figureF 18, figureG 14 = 134 pedestals (out/rip/GZLE01/godot/stage_data.json). Reached through the hatch on Forest Haven's outer rock (src/d/actor/d_a_obj_ohatch.cpp:1-4, src/d/actor/d_a_npc_kamome.cpp:570).
nintendo_gallery.actor: daNpcMt_c (Carlov), src/d/actor/d_a_npc_mt.cpp - FULLY DECOMPILED. The pedestals are daObjFigure_c, src/d/actor/d_a_obj_figure.cpp - also fully decompiled; both carry an identical copy of the figure table.
nintendo_gallery.cost: Free, but gated on hardware: the pictograph must be in colour. A greyscale shot (GX_TF_I4 or GX_TF_I8, i.e. the plain Picto Box) is rejected outright with the l_msg_mt_no_color table, so the Deluxe Picto Box is the real entry fee (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_mt.cpp:923-926).
rules: There are 0x86 = 134 figurine slots. Ownership is a bitfield spread over seventeen whole-byte event registers, figure N living in bit (N % 8) of register l_figure_comp[N / 8] (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_mt.cpp:14, 304-322, 1351-1374).

Carlov rejects a photo for four separate reasons, checked in this order: not colour -> l_msg_mt_no_color; subject not in the figure table (index <= DSNAP_TYPE_UNK48 or >= DSNAP_TYPE_UNKCF) -> l_msg_mt_no_figure; that figure already made -> l_msg_mt_maked; framing bad -> l_msg_mt_face_ng when getPictureResultDetail() == 1 and l_msg_mt_body_ng when it == 2 (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_mt.cpp:920-937).
A shipped bug: getPictureResultDetail() == 3 is never tested, so that detail code falls through into the accept branch (the decomp marks it !@bug at src/d/actor/d_a_npc_mt.cpp:938).

On accept, bits 0x2F01 and 0x3401 are set and register 0xA9FF stores the accepted photo index so the follow-up dialogue and the 'your figure is in room X' line can name it (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_mt.cpp:940-945, 900).
setFigure(n) ORs the bit and also sets bit 0x3A01, the 'you have made at least one figurine' flag that switches Carlov's dialogue tables (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_mt.cpp:1366-1375).

THE QUOTA: isComp() compares getFigureMakeNum() against 0x84 = 132, or against 0x85 = 133 when figure 0x32 has been made. Figure 0x32 is the conditional extra - the gallery is 'complete' at 132 figurines normally, 133 if that one is in it (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_mt.cpp:1390-1401).

Reaching the quota retires Carlov: on the next load of his room phase_1 sees isComp(), sets bit 0x3D08, calls setFigure(0x40) - which is Carlov's own figurine - and returns cPhs_STOP_e so the NPC is never created again (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_mt.cpp:386-414).

The 134 placed pedestals against the 132/133 quota is not a contradiction: two placed Figure actors are display-only or belong to the conditional pair, and figure 0x40 is granted by the completion code rather than photographed.
Each pedestal shows itself only when its own bit is set: daObjFigure_c::_create does mbDisplay = isFigureGet(mFigureNo) (src/d/actor/d_a_obj_figure.cpp:387, 989-999).

l_figure_room_name maps a figure to the stage it is displayed in: {Pfigure, figureA, figureB, figureC, figureD, figureE, figureF, figureG}, indexed by dSnap_GetFigRoomId(register 0xA9FF) (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_mt.cpp:324-333, 900).

TOTAL_FIGURE_COUNT.note: #define TOTAL_FIGURE_COUNT 0x86; the same define is repeated at src/d/actor/d_a_obj_figure.cpp:20

figure_bit_registers.note: l_figure_comp[N/8]; bit index is N%8. Seventeen bytes = 136 bits for 134 figures. Note the order is descending except for slots 10 and 11.

tiers.when: each accepted colour pictograph of a new subject
tiers.prize: one figurine displayed on its pedestal
tiers.bit: bit (N%8) of l_figure_comp[N/8]; plus 0x3A01 on the first one

tiers.when: 132 figurines (133 if figure 0x32 is among them)
tiers.prize: gallery complete - figure 0x40 (Carlov) is granted automatically and Carlov stops spawning

sinking_ships.name: Sinking Ships / Salvatore's Battleship - 'Sploosh Kaboom' (Kaisen, 'naval battle')
sinking_ships.stage: Kaisen, one room, reached from two SCLS doors inside Windfall (sea room 11 spawns 8 and 9). Placement is Kg1 at (-16, 0, 148), two KNOB00 doors, three item actors and four Fdai figurine pedestals; the game board is NOT placed and is created at runtime by Kg1 (out/rip/GZLE01/godot/stage_data.json:Kaisen).
sinking_ships.actor: daNpc_Kg1_c (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_kg1.cpp, 25 stub bodies) runs the counter; daMgBoard_c (src/d/actor/d_a_mgameboard.cpp, 14 stub bodies) is the board actor; but the RULES ENGINE dSeaFightGame_info_c (src/d/d_seafightgame.cpp, include/d/d_seafightgame.h) is FULLY DECOMPILED, and so is the board's small static file src/d/d_a_mgameboard_static.cpp.
sinking_ships.cost: UNRECOVERABLE. The entry fee is charged by daNpc_Kg1_c, whose every body is a stub. Nothing in src/ deducts rupees for this game. Do not invent a price.
rules: The board is 8x8. mGrid[8][8], cells hold 0 = untouched, 1 = missed shot, 3 = hit, and 102 + shipNo while a squid occupies them (src/d/d_seafightgame.cpp:11-15, 57-73, 105-127; include/d/d_seafightgame.h:23).

init(bulletNum, scenario) takes the shot allowance and one of three scenarios: scenario 1 = a single 2-cell squid; scenario 2 = a 2-cell and a 3-cell; scenario 3 = a 2-cell, a 3-cell and a 4-cell. mAliveShipNum is set to 1, 2 or 3 accordingly (src/d/d_seafightgame.cpp:10-40).

Squids are placed by rejection sampling: pick direction = rnd(1000) % 2, x = rnd(8), y = rnd(8), and retry until checkPutShip accepts. checkPutShip rejects when the squid would run off the 8x8 board or overlap a cell already holding a squid (value > 100) (src/d/d_seafightgame.cpp:42-103).

attack(x, y) returns -2 and costs NOTHING when the cell was already shot at - the game silently refuses to waste a bullet on a repeat. Otherwise it decrements mBulletNum and increments mScore, hit or miss (src/d/d_seafightgame.cpp:105-131).

THE SCORE IS SHOTS TAKEN, NOT HITS. mScore is incremented on every accepted shot regardless of outcome, so a LOWER score is a better result (src/d/d_seafightgame.cpp:128-129, src/d/d_a_mgameboard_static.cpp:15-17).
A squid dies when its cell counter field_0x9 reaches 0; mAliveShipNum then drops and mDeadShipNum rises (src/d/d_seafightgame.cpp:112-120).
The game is won when mAliveShipNum == 0 (daMgBoard_c::checkClearGame, src/d/d_a_mgameboard_static.cpp:9-12) and lost when the bullets run out.

getNearEnemy(x, y) is the proximity hint: it walks seven concentric square rings around the aimed cell (m_offset_1 .. m_offset_7, Chebyshev radius 1 to 7) and returns 1..7 for the first ring containing a squid, or 0 when the board is empty of squids within 7 cells. That is the 'you're getting warm' feedback (src/d/d_seafightgame.cpp:388-415).

cannon_game.name: Salvatore's cannon game (the barrel-shooting game)
cannon_game.stage: sea room 10 = dIsleRoom_SpectacleIsland_e (include/d/d_save.h:314). Kg2 stands at (-103529, 1057, -183445) and the Canon actor at (-103381, 1057, -183265), with two Kanban signboards on the beach. NOTE FOR THE BRIEF: this is Spectacle Island, not Bomb Island; there is exactly one Canon actor in the whole sea stage and one more in the E3ROOP demo stage (out/rip/GZLE01/godot/stage_data.json).
cannon_game.actor: daCanon_c, src/d/actor/d_a_canon.cpp - FULLY DECOMPILED, zero stub bodies. The NPC that talks you into it and hands out the prize, daNpc_Kg2_c, is 34 stub bodies.

rules: Ten shots, five targets. wait_proc arms the game the moment the event cut named 'Canon_game' starts: it calls createTargetObj(), sets m65A = 0 hits and m65C = 10 shots, teleports the player 200 units back along the cannon's home angle, and calls dComIfGp_startMiniGame(3) (src/d/actor/d_a_canon.cpp:251-281).

The five targets are barrels dropped on a random 8x8 polar grid in front of the cannon. createTargetObj loops until it has five accepted cells: each candidate is (rnd(8), rnd(8)) and createCheck rejects it if the COLUMN index already belongs to an earlier target - so no two targets ever share a bearing (src/d/actor/d_a_canon.cpp:139-150, 173-184).

getGridPos maps a grid cell to a world position: distance = row * 1500 + 10500, bearing = home.angle.y + angle_y_tbl[column], and the y is snapped to the sea wave height. angle_y_tbl spans -0x1200 to +0x1200 in eight steps, so the targets occupy a 50-degree fan from 10500 to 21000 units out (src/d/actor/d_a_canon.cpp:29-30, 117-125).

The targets are Obj_Barrel2 children created with params 0x037F003F: type 3 (the mine/target variant), itemSave 0x7F, itemNo 0x3F which is the 'no item' code, buoy 0 so each carries a marker flag (src/d/actor/d_a_canon.cpp:180; param layout at include/d/actor/d_a_obj_barrel2.h:50-70).

Aiming (PadMove): yaw is clamped to home.angle.y +/- 0x1200 (about 25 degrees each way) and pitch to the band [home.angle.x, home.angle.x + 0x1000] (about 22.5 degrees). Stick deflection past 0.5 moves the target angle by up to 0x400 per frame in yaw and 512 in pitch, and shape_angle chases it with cLib_addCalcAngleS(.., 4, 0x100, 0x10) (src/d/actor/d_a_canon.cpp:449-490).

Firing: A fires. The shot's flight time in frames is m652 = ((home.angle.x + 0x1000) - shape_angle.x) / 0x1000 * 56 + 64, i.e. 64 frames at maximum elevation up to 120 frames at minimum - a flatter shot flies longer. The landing distance is the same ratio * 10500 + 10500, so range runs from 10500 to 21000 units, exactly the span the targets occupy (src/d/actor/d_a_canon.cpp:128-136, 329-339).
The shell follows a parabola: its height above the chord is scaled by 1 - 4*(t - 0.5)^2 where t is the fraction of flight remaining (src/d/actor/d_a_canon.cpp:341-346).
m65C is decremented at the moment of firing, and the corresponding 2D shot icon is greyed out (src/d/actor/d_a_canon.cpp:337-338).

Landing: a 30-frame pause. If the shell's collision cylinder hit, m65A is incremented, a target icon is greyed out, and dComIfGp_setMiniGameRupee(m65A) republishes the HIT COUNT - so the on-screen number is hits, not rupees (src/d/actor/d_a_canon.cpp:370-379).

Three end sounds are played on Kg2: JA_SE_PLAYSPOT_END_S on the fifth hit, JA_SE_PLAYSPOT_END_F when the shots run out, and JA_SE_PLAYSPOT_DESTROY on any ordinary hit (src/d/actor/d_a_canon.cpp:380-392).
The game continues only while m65C > 0 AND m65A < 5; otherwise end_proc_init runs (src/d/actor/d_a_canon.cpp:400-406).

OUTCOME: 5 hits out of 5 sets dComIfGp_setMiniGameResult(1) and daNpc_Kg2_c::setCanonGameResult(1). Anything else sets (2, 2). There is no partial-credit tier inside daCanon_c (src/d/actor/d_a_canon.cpp:410-424).
60 frames later end_proc destroys every remaining target barrel (breakAllObj spawns a bomb on each) and calls dComIfGp_endMiniGame(3) (src/d/actor/d_a_canon.cpp:186-199, 426-447).
SHIPPED BUG: CreateHeap fills m5AC using ARRAY_SSIZE(m584) = 10 although m5AC has only 5 elements, overrunning the array by five pointers (src/d/actor/d_a_canon.cpp:535-545, the decomp marks it Bug).

THE COURSE IS WORTH EXACTLY 150 RUPEES. The 38 Ktarur barrels in Ocean decode (itemNo = params & 0x3F) to 20 barrels holding a Green Rupee (1), 11 holding a Yellow Rupee (10), 1 holding a Red Rupee (20) and 6 holding item 0x3F = nothing. 20*1 + 11*10 + 1*20 = 150, which is exactly l_HIO.mPerfectRupeeScore. The six empty barrels are type 2, the mine variant, and they are the ones that get a marker flag (prm_get_buoy() == 0) (out/rip/GZLE01/godot/stage_data.json:Ocean; include/d/actor/d_a_obj_barrel2.h:50-70; src/d/actor/d_a_obj_barrel2.cpp:272-296).

The finish line is a pair of path points: daGoal_Flag_c reads points 0 and 1 of the path named in params >> 16 into mGoalFlagPolePos[0..1] and remembers which side of that line the player started on (src/d/actor/d_a_goal_flag.cpp:550-600).

goal_check() returns +1 for crossing the line the right way and -1 for crossing it backwards. The FIRST correct crossing only sets mRaceEndState = 1 (it is the start line); the SECOND correct crossing ends the race - with 0 rupees collected it is a failure (state 2), otherwise a finish (state 3) (src/d/actor/d_a_goal_flag.cpp:800-808).

Three ways to lose, all ending at race_fail_cam: the clock reaching 0, crossing the line backwards, and crossing the finish having collected nothing. All three play JA_SE_SGAME_TIMER_0 or fall to minigame result 2 and BGM JA_BGM_SEA_FAIL (src/d/actor/d_a_goal_flag.cpp:800-820).

A finish is classified by rupees: fewer than mPerfectRupeeScore = 150 is finish_type 1, otherwise finish_type 2 = perfect. The MiniGameTerminater is created with (finish_type, remaining_time = getRestTimeMs()/10, rupees_collected) (src/d/actor/d_a_goal_flag.cpp:826-847).

The results camera can be skipped with A, B or START, but only after l_HIO.mEndCamEarlyFrame = 150 frames (5 seconds). Either way it ends with dComIfGp_setNextStage("sea", 1, dIsleRoom_BoatingCourse_e) - back onto the dock in front of Sarace (src/d/actor/d_a_goal_flag.cpp:869-899).

A mid-race restart (falling out of the course) is special-cased in the player: daPy_lk_c::startRestartRoom sees minigame type 1, forces the same next stage, plays JA_SE_FORCE_BACK and writes ship_race_result = 3 (src/d/actor/d_a_player_main.cpp:10855-10866).

DELIBERATE INVERSION: _delete maps minigame result 1 (the ordinary finish) to ship_race_result 2 and result 2 (the failure) to ship_race_result 1, carrying the rupee count across in both cases. Do not 'fix' this when porting (src/d/actor/d_a_goal_flag.cpp:713-730).

salvage_corp.name: Salvage - hauling sunken treasure up with the Grappling Hook (the Salvage Corp's trade)
salvage_corp.stage: The whole Great Sea. 449 salvage markers are placed across stages sea / sea_r11 / sea_r44 under five object names, all mapping to fpcNm_Salvage_e (src/d/d_stage.cpp:535-540). The Salvage Corp's own barge is a daObjIkada_c ship type, not a game actor (src/d/actor/d_a_obj_ikada.cpp:1-4).
salvage_corp.actor: daSalvage_c, src/d/actor/d_a_salvage.cpp (one stub body out of 771 lines) plus its data class dSalvage_control_c, src/d/d_salvage.cpp - FULLY DECOMPILED. The chest that surfaces is daSTBox_c, src/d/actor/d_a_salvage_tbox.cpp - fully decompiled.
salvage_corp.cost: No rupee cost. The cost is equipment and time: the ship must be in crane mode with the Grappling Hook out (daShip_c::checkCraneMode()), and the hook has to be winched down past a depth threshold.
rules: Salvage markers are registered into a single 160-slot table: 128 slots for sea-grid markers and 32 for room markers (dSalvage_control_c::MAX_SEA = 128, MAX_ROOM = 32, include/d/d_salvage.h:69-73). Markers are re-registered every time the room changes.

Marker parameters (src/d/d_salvage.cpp:12-20): kind = params >> 28, saveNo = params >> 20 & 0xFF, roomNo = params >> 12 & 0xFF, itemNo = params >> 4 & 0xFF, type = params & 0x0F, switchNo = home.angle.z & 0xFF, and for kind 0 the candidate index = home.angle.z & 0x03.
SIX KINDS, and they are the whole taxonomy of Wind Waker salvage (src/d/d_salvage.cpp:87-112, src/d/actor/d_a_salvage.cpp:276-340, 503-530):

kind 0 - a Treasure Chart point. saveNo is the chart number 1..49 (validated 1..128). It only exists once the chart is opened and not yet completed; hauling it sets dComIfGs_onCompleteCollectMap(saveNo) and event bit 0x3E02. Triforce Charts additionally need dComIfGs_isCollectMapTriforce(itemNo - 0x60) before the point becomes active.
kind 2 - a switch-gated point (saveNo validated 0..15). If the switch belongs to a Big Octo the marker is dragged to the octo's live position each frame; hauling it sets the ocean save bit.
kind 3 - a plain sea point remembered by dComIfGs_onOceanSvBit(roomNo, saveNo).
kind 4 - the same, but only active in daylight: clrFlag while dKy_daynight_check() != DAY, setFlag during the day.
kind 5 - a blank. checkDistance keeps it as a LAST RESORT only, returning any other overlapping marker first, and checkOrder routes it to the SALVAGE_HAZURE ('miss') event instead of SALVAGE_GETITEM.

kind 6 - a moon-gated point. Active only when !dKy_moon_type_chk() && dKyr_moon_arrival_check() && the matching bit in daSalvage_c::m_savelabel[saveNo] is clear; hauling it sets that bit rather than an ocean bit, and the marker is NOT re-initialised afterwards.

THE TREASURE-CHART POINTS ARE RANDOMISED PER SAVE FILE. Each of the 49 chart numbers is placed FOUR times, at four different spots, distinguished by home.angle.z & 0x03 = 0, 1, 2, 3. Only the candidate whose index equals dSv_player_info_c::mRandomSalvagePoint is registered at all; the other three are dropped in dSalvage_control_c::entry (src/d/d_salvage.cpp:13, 89-95; include/d/d_save.h:457-468). Cross-checked in the placement data: 47 charts have exactly 4 placements and 2 have 8.

REACH: the grapple's tip must be inside the marker's XZ radius AND at least a randomised depth below the water surface. checkArea uses l_salvage_depth = {1000, 1500, 2000} indexed by mRndDepthIdx, which is re-rolled as rnd(10000) % 3 every time the crane leaves every marker's XZ radius - so how deep you have to dig changes from attempt to attempt (src/d/actor/d_a_salvage.cpp:348-350, 442-463).

RADIUS AND HEIGHT come from the placement scale, per kind: kind 0 gets R = scale.x * 700 and H = scale.y * 1000; kind 5 gets R = scale.x * 500, H = scale.y * 1000; every other kind gets R = scale.x * 400, H = scale.y * 500 (src/d/d_salvage.cpp:125-138).
The proximity chime JA_SE_OBJ_SALVAGE_TAG plays within 5000 units of an active marker of an effect-bearing kind (src/d/actor/d_a_salvage.cpp:341-343).

Four outcomes are ordered depending on marker type and which way the crane is turned: type 1 splits on ship->getCraneAngle() < 0 into m2E9 1 or 2, and kinds 5 / types 0,2,3 into m2E9 3 or 4, selecting between SALVAGE_GETITEM, the left-hand variant, SALVAGE_HAZURE and the plain event (src/d/actor/d_a_salvage.cpp:353-372, 168-240).

The chest that comes up is fpcNm_SALVAGE_TBOX_e created with params (type << 8) | itemNo; it hands over the item with fopAcM_createItemForTrBoxDemo (src/d/actor/d_a_salvage.cpp:195-197; src/d/actor/d_a_salvage_tbox.cpp:217, 370, 440).
A blank can bite back: daSalvage_c::createEnemy() spawns an Octorok (fpcNm_OQ_e, subtype 2) on top of the player (src/d/actor/d_a_salvage.cpp:466-470; src/d/d_stage.cpp:806).
Ghost-ship style markers can be re-homed onto a moving daOship_c by matching switch numbers (onSalvageForOship, src/d/actor/d_a_salvage.cpp:473-499).

rules: A HARD RULE THAT IS EASY TO MISS: enemies in the Savage Labyrinth drop NOTHING. fopAcM_createIball returns fpcM_ERROR_PROCESS_ID_e immediately when the start stage name is Cave09, Cave10 or Cave11, before the drop roll is even made - so no hearts, no rupees, no arrows from anything you kill in there (src/f_op/f_op_actor_mng.cpp:1239-1244).

Each room holds exactly ONE Pitfall hole, and every single one of the 61 placed holes has exitIdx 0 with the model flag set. daObj_Hole_c::modeWait triggers when the player is within l_HIO.m08 * scale.x + mScaleLocal*10 of it, plays the DEFAULT_PITFALL event, and then calls dLib_setNextStageBySclsNum(0, current.roomNo) - i.e. the destination is SCLS entry 0 of the CURRENT ROOM's own dzr, not of the stage dzs (src/d/actor/d_a_obj_hole.cpp:96-136, 233-246).

That is why the floor chain does not appear in the ripped stage report: out/rip/GZLE01/stages/Cave09/Cave09_report.json:exits is empty because it lists stage-level SCLS only. Reading each room dzr's SCLS[0] would recover the exact floor order; that is the open lead for this minigame.
Hole census: Cave09 has a hole in all 21 rooms; Cave10 in rooms 0..19 (room 20 has the chest and a warp instead); Cave11 in rooms 0..9 and 11..20 (room 10 has a warp instead).

Cave10 room 17 is the only room in the three stages with an ALLdie: daAlldie_c polls fopAcM_myRoomSearchEnemy every frame, and once the room has been enemy-free for 65 consecutive frames it calls dComIfGs_onSwitch(params >> 8, roomNo). Everywhere else the 'clear the room to open the way' logic is not in a decompiled actor (src/d/actor/d_a_alldie.cpp:18-48, 68-80).

The Ysdls00 warp lights are the rest / bail-out points. Cave09 has them in rooms 0, 15 and 20; Cave10 in rooms 0, 15 and 20; Cave11 in rooms 0, 10, 15 and 20. Their params are 0x10FF01E0 (room 0 everywhere), 0x10FF01FF (the mid-stage ones), 0x10FF010C (Cave09 room 20) and 0x10FF000E (Cave10 room 20). daWarpls_c has no decompiled body at all, so this parameter layout is NOT decoded here; the raw values are recorded so a remake can match them later.
Room 0 of each stage carries no fight actors beyond a Piwa and a pot in Cave09 - it is the arrival room.
The rooms are otherwise pure enemy arenas: bonbori lamps (26 / 29 / 48), Zenfire flame jets (18 / 18 / 17), SW_C00 switch objects (11 / 12 / 9) and CmTrap spike traps (6, Cave10 only).

fishman_charts.stage: The Great Sea, one Fishman per sea grid: 49 NpcSo actors in stage sea, one more in sea_r44 and one in sea_r11, alongside 245 TagSo marker tags in sea (out/rip/GZLE01/godot/stage_data.json). 49 is exactly dIsleIdx_COUNT_e (include/d/d_save.h:407).
fishman_charts.actor: daNpc_So_c, src/d/actor/d_a_npc_so.cpp - 72 stub bodies out of 450 lines. Its helper tag daTag_So_c (src/d/actor/d_a_tag_so.cpp) IS fully decompiled but holds only a volume, no rules.

rules: RULES LARGELY UNRECOVERABLE - daNpc_So_c is a stub. What follows is the storage and the wiring, which ARE recoverable, plus an honest list of what is not.

THE SEA CHART STORAGE: dSv_player_map_c::mFmapBits[dIsleIdx_COUNT_e] is one byte per sea grid, 49 grids. Bit 0 is set by onSaveArriveGrid(no) and read by isSaveArriveGrid(no); bit 1 is the separate GBA-link copy set by onSaveArriveGridForAgb (include/d/d_save.h:425-432, src/d/d_save.cpp:929-960). The array is the per-quadrant 'this square of the chart is filled in' state, and it has six spare bits per grid.

NOTHING IN THE DECOMPILED TREE CALLS onSaveArriveGrid OR onFmapBit for gameplay. The only caller of anything in that family is d_map.cpp:1796 -> onSaveArriveGridForAgbUseGridPos, the GBA link. Whatever the Fishman writes when he draws in your chart is inside the stub. Do not invent a bit index.

The Fishman's talk-and-feed sequence is visible only as symbol names: _searchEsa (find the bait), _searchTagSo / _searchMinigameTagSo (find his marker volumes), modeEventEsaInit/modeEventEsa (eat), modeEventMapopenInit/modeEventMapopen (draw the chart), modeEventBowInit/modeEventBow (the bow game), modeGetRupeeInit/modeGetRupee, modeEventTriForceInit/modeEventTriForce (include/d/actor/d_a_npc_so.h:19-77).

THE TEN-ARROW GAME. include/d/actor/d_a_npc_so.h:15 defines getMiniGameRestArrow() { return 10 - mB78; }, so mB78 counts arrows used and the allowance is 10. src/d/d_meter.cpp:2472-2482 draws it: while dComIfGp_getMiniGameType() == 8 it finds the NPC_SO actor, hides the tens pane when the count is below 10 and always shows the units pane. No decompiled code ever calls startMiniGame(8), and the whole cutMiniGame* family (cutMiniGameStart, cutMiniGameWaitProc, cutMiniGamePlTurnProc, cutMiniGamePlUpProc, cutMiniGameWarpProc, cutMiniGameReturnProc, cutMiniGameEndProc, include/d/actor/d_a_npc_so.h:102-115) is stubbed, so the scoring, the targets and the prize are all invisible.

TagSo marker volumes ARE decoded: params bits 0-7 are the marker id, bits 8-15 a radius multiplied by 100 (0xFF meaning the default 1600), bits 16-23 a mode byte where 1 draws a debug fan of half-angle 0x3500 around shape_angle.y. The actor has no execute logic at all - it is pure data for the Fishman to find (src/d/actor/d_a_tag_so.cpp:40-63).

245 TagSo against 49 Fishmen is about five markers per Fishman - consistent with _searchTagSo picking a swim target and _searchMinigameTagSo picking a game target, but that mapping is not stated anywhere.

rito_mail_sorting.name: Koboli's letter-sorting game (Dragon Roost postal service) - BONUS, not on the original brief; found because it owns event register 0x8AFF
rito_mail_sorting.stage: Dragon Roost Island's post office. Koboli is the Bmsw actor (fpcNm_NPC_BMSW_e, src/d/d_stage.cpp:721); once the game is finished with he is replaced at spawn time by Btsw (fpcNm_NPC_BTSW_e, src/d/d_stage.cpp:722).
rito_mail_sorting.actor: daNpc_Bmsw_c, src/d/actor/d_a_npc_bmsw.cpp - FULLY DECOMPILED, zero stub bodies (1709 lines). daNpc_Btsw_c is the post-game replacement and is also decompiled.
rules: Four lessons, tracked in event register 0xC203 - byte 0xC2, mask 0x03, values 0..3. daNpc_Bmsw_c::_create checks it on spawn: at value 3 with bit 0x2701 still clear it deletes itself and creates Btsw in its place (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_bmsw.cpp:1134-1145).

Each round is a timer: dTimer_createTimer(6, l_HIO.field_0x30, 3, 4, 221, l_HIO.field_0x48, 32, l_HIO.field_0x4C) with field_0x30 = 0x1E = 30, then dComIfG_TimerStart(6, l_HIO.field_0x32) with field_0x32 = 0x0F = 15. The 30 is the round length in the same unit daGoal_Flag_c uses for its 240-second race timer, i.e. seconds; the 15 is the start mode. field_0x34 = 0x3C = 60 is set but not used by this call (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_bmsw.cpp:80-110, 899-913).
dComIfGp_setMiniGameRupee(0) then dComIfGp_startMiniGame(7); the minigame counter is the LETTER COUNT, not rupees (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_bmsw.cpp:904-905).

PASS MARKS, per lesson (daNpc_Bmsw_getGameEndMsg, src/d/actor/d_a_npc_bmsw.cpp:185-244): lesson 0 passes at 10 letters, lesson 1 at 20, lesson 2 at 25. Passing advances the register - message 0x1A38 sets it to 1, 0x1A4D sets it to 2, 0x1A58 sets it to 3 (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_bmsw.cpp:425-447).

PAYOUT, per lesson (setGameGetRupee, src/d/actor/d_a_npc_bmsw.cpp:808-848): lesson 0 pays nothing below 10 letters and letters/2 at or above 10. Lesson 1 pays nothing below 15, letters/2 from 15 to 19, and letters at 20 or more. Lesson 2 pays nothing below 20, letters from 20 to 24, and letters x 3 at 25 or more. Lesson 3 pays letters x 3 while bit 0x2701 is clear and only letters once it is set. The halving is written as rupees >> 1, which the decomp notes does not match rupees / 2 - so it is an arithmetic shift, and negative counts would round the other way.
The payout is handed over with dComIfGp_setItemRupeeCount(field_0x960) at the specific message numbers 0x1A39 / 0x1A4E / 0x1A5F / 0x1A59 / 0x1A6F (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_bmsw.cpp:731-740).

Once bit 0x2701 is set (Koboli's mother's letter has been delivered - daNpc_Btsw_c does this in the GETMOTHERLETTER event) the game becomes an endless high-score run: register 0x8AFF holds the record, a run beats it only with rupees > the record (rupees <= record plays the 'you did not beat it' message), and beating it overwrites the register (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_bmsw.cpp:226-238).

The record register 0x8AFF is SEEDED AT 25 by daNpc_Btsw_c when the mother's letter event ends, together with bit 0x2701 - so the freeplay record starts at the lesson-2 pass mark (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_btsw.cpp:872-874).
The record is printed into text by the message system (src/f_op/f_op_msg_mng.cpp:2349, 4344, 6366, 8032).
Two different events run the round: SHIWAKEGAME before bit 0x2701 and SHIWAKEGAME2 after (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_bmsw.cpp:889-895).
Side bits: 0x1A02 marks the very first conversation, 0x1A01 marks 'the rules have been explained / declined once' (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_bmsw.cpp:401, 427-431, 527-533).
